name: Monitor and manage direct private equity portfolio companies
summary: After a direct private equity deal closes, the deal team owns the holding until exit. Each quarter the team reads the company's monthly and quarter-end management accounts, talks to the CFO, updates its model and covenant headroom, sends valuation inputs to the independent valuation group, prepares the fund's director for the board meeting and takes positions on budgets, add-on acquisitions and refinancings. Most holdings are owned alongside a lead sponsor or partner, so the fund often has a board seat but not control, and about a third are passive co-investments followed through the sponsor's reports. Company packs arrive in different formats and are re-keyed into spreadsheets, board timing is set by the company, and the work competes with new deals for the same people.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian public pension investment manager whose Private Equity department holds about 150 to 170 direct investments, mostly alongside sponsors and partners.
baseline.notes: Direct private equity groups in North America, Europe and Asia plus passive co-investments in Funds and Secondaries. Portfolio Value Creation in Real Assets supports material holdings.

trigger: The first monthly management pack of the quarter arrives from an active holding (or the lead sponsor's quarterly report for a passive co-investment), a newly closed holding is handed over, or a value creation plan is launched.
end_state: The quarter's monitoring note is filed with valuation inputs sent to Valuations and board decisions recorded, or an exit proposal is sent to the exit process.

volume.seasonality: Work bunches in the six weeks after each quarter end (quarter-end packs, valuation inputs, board meetings); budget approvals fall in the quarter before the company's fiscal year starts.

evidence.note: Process map volume of about 150 holding-quarters a quarter; PE reported 152 direct investments in F2020 and 166 in F2021, of which 85 and 88 were DPE holdings.

Reviews monthly and quarterly reporting, keeps the monitoring model, records board actions and handles passive co-investments. Estimated from hands-on time (about 15 hours per holding-quarter averaged over the mix) times 50 holding-quarters a month.
Reviews the quarterly update, drafts valuation inputs, board briefing notes, decision analyses and exit proposals. Estimated from hands-on time times volume.
Leads monthly CFO calls and watch-list remediation. Estimated from hands-on time; principals also spend unrecorded time on informal calls with management.
Sits on the board of active holdings, reads board packs and attends meetings. Estimated from about 6 hours per board meeting times about 28 board meetings a month.
Approves shareholder positions on reserved matters and chairs the quarterly portfolio review. Estimated from hands-on time times volume.

roles.title: Associate, PE portfolio and business management
roles.department: PE strategy, portfolio and business management

evidence.note: Consolidates holdings into the department's quarterly portfolio report. Estimated at about 30 minutes per holding.
Reviews value creation plan progress for material holdings. Estimated from about 2 hours for one holding in three among active holdings.

systems.name: Deal pipeline and relationship management system
Cloud enterprise data platform and data warehouse
Document management and investment committee memo repository
Bloomberg terminals, market data and trade messaging
Private investments administration and cash flow system

steps.name: Log the incoming report and route the holding
steps.description: The associate covering the holding saves the company's first monthly management pack of the quarter (or, for a passive co-investment, the lead sponsor's quarterly company report) to the deal folder, logs its arrival date against the reporting deadline in the shareholder agreement and routes the holding as newly closed, active board-seat or passive.
inputs: monthly management pack or sponsor's quarterly report

next.condition: newly closed holding handed over from the closing team
active holding with a board seat or material governance rights
passive or minority co-investment without a board seat

evidence.note: Mix estimated from 166 PE direct investments (F2021), of which 88 are DPE holdings, plus passive co-investments up to C$100 million; new holdings about 5% of holding-quarters from the net growth of 14 directs a year plus replacements for exits.

steps.name: Set up monitoring for a newly closed company
steps.description: The senior associate turns the diligence model and investment thesis into a monitoring template, agrees the monthly pack contents, KPI schedule and reporting deadlines with the company CFO, loads the board calendar, and records the value creation plan baseline and reserved matters that need the fund's consent.

error.defect_description: KPI definitions or covenant thresholds set up wrongly in the template.

evidence.note: Onboarding and monitoring practices described in the 2022 Report on Sustainable Investing; KPI schedule tied to the thesis from the sponsor reporting guide. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct private equity holding.

steps.name: Review month-one management accounts against budget
steps.description: The associate compares revenue, EBITDA, cash conversion, capital expenditure and net debt with budget and the prior year, reads management's variance commentary, updates the monthly tab of the monitoring model and lists questions for the CFO call.

error.defect_description: A variance or covenant pressure point is missed.

evidence.note: Monthly management pack with variance commentary 10 to 20 business days after month end. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct private equity holding.

steps.name: Re-key monthly figures into the portfolio dashboard
steps.description: The associate copies the headline monthly figures and KPIs from the company's spreadsheet or PDF into the department's portfolio monitoring template and dashboard, because company packs come in different formats and are not fed automatically.

error.defect_description: Keying error or figure taken from the wrong column.

evidence.note: Manual assembly of KPI reports from several systems in Excel described by the CVCA article. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct private equity holding.

steps.name: Hold the monthly call with the company CFO
steps.description: The principal, with the associate listening in, walks through the variances, cash, trading outlook, pipeline and any issues with the CFO, and records agreed follow-ups and anything the board should hear early.

evidence.note: Monthly operational calls between sponsors and management described in the board handbook. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct private equity holding.

steps.name: Review month-two management accounts
steps.description: When the second monthly pack of the quarter arrives, the associate repeats the budget and prior-year comparison, updates the model and dashboard in one pass, and escalates to the principal only if results or cash moved materially.

error.defect_description: A trend in working capital or margins is missed.

evidence.note: Wait is the gap until the next monthly pack, 10 to 20 business days after the next month end. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct private equity holding.

steps.name: Wait for quarter-end results from the company
steps.description: The company closes its quarter and sends quarter-end management accounts, the KPI schedule and, where it has debt, the covenant compliance calculation; late or restated packs are chased by email.

evidence.note: Full packs 10 to 20 business days after period end; covenant certificates often 45 days after quarter end. Wait counted from the month-two review.

steps.name: Update the quarterly model, covenant headroom and KPI dashboard
steps.description: The associate rolls the model to the quarter end: last-twelve-month EBITDA, net debt and leverage against covenants, progress against the value creation plan milestones, KPIs from the investment thesis, and a refreshed forecast for the year.

error.defect_description: Roll-forward or formula error in the model.

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct private equity holding.

steps.name: Review the quarterly update and send valuation inputs to Valuations
steps.description: The senior associate checks the model against the company's accounts, writes a short performance commentary and assembles the valuation input pack (last-twelve-month and budget EBITDA, net debt, comparable companies and recent transactions) for the Finance valuation group by the valuation calendar deadline.

error.defect_description: A one-off item is left in EBITDA used for valuation.

control.basis: Valuation policy and calendar: deal teams supply quarter-end valuation inputs to the independent valuation group by its deadline

next.condition: errors or gaps sent back to the associate

evidence.note: Finance values private holdings independently each quarter; IPEV requires fair value at each measurement date with calibration; GIPS requires quarterly valuation of private market investments. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct private equity holding.

steps.name: Wait for the board pack
steps.description: Company management prepares the board pack (quarterly results, strategy updates, decisions sought) and circulates it on the board portal or by email a few days before the meeting; some quarters have no formal meeting.

next.condition: no formal board meeting this quarter

evidence.note: Boards meet every 6 to 8 weeks at most firms and at least four times a year; packs go out 3 to 7 days before the meeting.

steps.name: Prepare the board briefing note for the fund's director
steps.description: The senior associate reads the board pack, reconciles it to the monitoring model, and writes a briefing note with the issues to raise, questions for management and a recommended position on each resolution.

evidence.note: Directors need at least two hours to read the pack; principals prepare internal materials on portfolio company updates. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct private equity holding.

steps.name: Attend the board meeting and vote
steps.description: The director nominated by the fund reads the pack and briefing note, attends the meeting in person or by video, challenges management on performance and plans, and votes on resolutions within the fund's agreed positions.

next.condition: routine meeting with no reserved matter needing the fund's consent
budget, add-on acquisition, refinancing, dividend or management change needs the fund's position

evidence.note: Meetings run 2 to 4 hours plus reading time; boards of 5 to 7 members. Share of quarters with a decision item covers the annual budget sign-off (one quarter in four) plus other reserved matters.

steps.name: Analyse the decision item and draft the fund's position
steps.description: The senior associate analyses the proposal (next year's budget, an add-on acquisition model, new debt terms, a dividend recapitalisation or a management incentive plan), tests it against the investment case and drafts a recommendation for the group head.

error.defect_description: Downside case or financing terms not fully tested.

evidence.note: Add-on acquisitions and management changes are leading value levers; budget calendar from the board handbook. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct private equity holding.

steps.name: Approve the fund's position on the reserved matter
steps.description: The group head reviews the decision note, may call the director and company CEO, and approves how the fund will vote or consent; any request for new equity from the fund is sent to the investment committees as a follow-on.

control.basis: Investment Management Authorities: group head approval of shareholder positions on reserved matters; follow-on investments need IDC or PEC approval

next.condition: proposal needs new equity from the fund

evidence.note: Investment Management Authorities set approval authorities; IDC and PEC approve follow-on transactions. Shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Open a follow-on opportunity in the deal pipeline
steps.description: The associate records the follow-on request (add-on funding, rescue equity or a partner's stake for sale) as a new opportunity in the pipeline system so that it goes through screening, diligence and committee approval like a new deal.

evidence.note: Follow-ons are approved by committees (src1, src2) but the process map has no link from this process to deal screening; the author assumes a pipeline entry.

steps.name: Record board decisions and actions
steps.description: The associate writes up the board outcome, the fund's votes and follow-up actions in the holding's monitoring file and updates the dashboard flags (watch items, covenant headroom, value creation milestones).

next.condition: material holding with an active value creation plan
annual sustainability data cycle falls in this quarter

evidence.note: Write-up practice is the author's estimate; share with value creation plans from PVC working on material direct equity investments (src2).

steps.name: Review value creation plan progress with Portfolio Value Creation
steps.description: The PVC principal and the deal team review milestones in the value creation plan (pricing, procurement, digital and data projects, management hires), agree changes and send the updated plan back to the deal team and company.

next.condition: annual sustainability data cycle falls in this quarter

evidence.note: PVC strengthens value creation planning and monitoring; operating partners join post-investment value creation in 51% of deals in the survey. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct private equity holding.

steps.name: Collect annual sustainability, cyber and climate updates
steps.description: Once a year the associate sends the company the sustainability KPI template (health, safety and environment, emissions, diversity and other core metrics), the cyber maturity questions and, where climate risk is material, the climate scenario update, then checks and files the answers with Sustainable Investing.

error.defect_description: Company reports metrics on a different basis from the template.

control.basis: Policy on Sustainable Investing: monitoring of material sustainability factors in assets with material governance rights

evidence.note: Proprietary sustainability KPI framework for direct equity investments (fiscal 2022), cyber maturity assessments, climate framework applied to existing assets and the ESG Data Convergence Initiative. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct private equity holding.

steps.name: Consolidate the holding into the department's quarterly portfolio report
steps.description: The business management associate pulls the holding's figures, valuation movement and flags from the dashboard into the department's quarterly portfolio report and checks that every holding has reported.

evidence.note: Department-level portfolio reporting by the PE business management team is the author's assumption based on the organisation file's unit purpose.

steps.name: Review the holding at the quarterly portfolio review
steps.description: The group head and department leaders review each holding's performance against plan, valuation change and risks in a portfolio review meeting and decide to hold, put it on the watch list or start preparing an exit.

evidence.note: Holding periods of about five years imply about 5% of holdings reaching exit in a quarter; the process map gives about 3 PE exits a month against 50 holding-quarters (6%). Watch-list share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run the watch-list remediation plan
steps.description: The principal steps up contact with the company: weekly cash reviews, lender discussions on covenant resets, management changes or PVC support, and reports progress to the group head until the holding comes off the watch list.

evidence.note: Remediation effort is the author's estimate; COVID-19 in 2020 put many holdings through this path.

steps.name: Draft the exit proposal
steps.description: The senior associate sets out exit options (sale to a strategic or sponsor buyer, listing, sale to a partner), timing against the business plan and market windows, expected proceeds against the latest valuation, and the partner's view, then files the note and sends the proposal to the exit process.

evidence.note: A high-value exit is a leading value lever; DPE supported two IPOs and sold holdings in fiscal 2021. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct private equity holding.

steps.name: File the quarterly monitoring note
steps.description: The associate files the quarter's monitoring note (results, valuation inputs, board summary, actions) in the document system and updates the holding's status in the pipeline and portfolio systems.

evidence.note: Filing practice is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the sponsor's quarterly report on a passive co-investment
steps.description: For a passive co-investment the associate reads the lead sponsor's company report and capital account, compares results and the sponsor's value with the prior quarter and the original case, and notes questions for the sponsor's next investor call.

evidence.note: Funds and Secondaries makes minority, passive direct investments alongside fund partners. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct private equity holding.

steps.name: Update the co-investment record and send valuation inputs
steps.description: The associate keys the headline figures and the sponsor's reported value into the dashboard and sends them, with the sponsor report, to the valuation group.

error.defect_description: Sponsor value taken at the wrong reference date.

evidence.note: Finance values private holdings each quarter; sponsor-reported values are a starting point under IPEV. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct private equity holding.

exceptions.name: Late or restated company pack
exceptions.description: The company misses its reporting deadline or restates a month; the associate chases and the quarter-end model and valuation inputs are held up.

exceptions.name: Reserved matter needing the fund's consent
exceptions.description: The board asks for a budget sign-off, add-on, refinancing, dividend or management change and the group head must approve the fund's position.

exceptions.name: Follow-on equity request
exceptions.description: The company or partner asks the fund for new equity, which leaves this process as a new pipeline opportunity needing committee approval.

exceptions.name: Watch list
exceptions.description: Results or liquidity deteriorate and the principal runs a remediation plan with management and lenders.

exceptions.name: Exit preparation
exceptions.description: The quarterly portfolio review decides to prepare a sale or listing and an exit proposal goes to the exit process.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the first monthly pack of the quarter (or sponsor report) to the quarterly monitoring note filed
benchmarks.population: Active and passive direct private equity holdings of a large pension investor

evidence.note: Author's reading: the first monthly pack arrives about 20 days into the second month, quarter-end packs 10 to 20 business days after quarter end, board meetings every 6 to 8 weeks, and valuation inputs must arrive in time for statements due 45 days after quarter end. Passive holdings take about two weeks.
Practitioner handbook.

benchmarks.value: 5 to 7 members in over 90% of portfolio companies

evidence.note: Table 15a.
Operating partners involved in identifying post-investment value sources in 51% of deals; consultants in 27%.

pain_points.description: Company packs arrive in different formats and are re-keyed into spreadsheets and the dashboard, which takes associate time and introduces keying errors.
Quarter-end packs arrive two to four weeks after quarter end while valuation inputs are due soon after, so the model update and valuation pack are squeezed.
Board dates are set by the company and the lead sponsor; packs often arrive only a few days before the meeting, leaving little time to brief the director.
As a minority co-owner the fund can only influence some decisions through its board seat and consent rights, and passive co-investments depend on the sponsor's reporting.

evidence.note: DPE invests alongside aligned partners; F&S co-investments are passive.

pain_points.description: The same deal professionals run new deals, so monitoring work waits behind live transactions.

evidence.note: Author's judgment; the organisation does not split time by activity.

sources.title: The model fund F2022 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2022)
sources.supports: The Portfolio Execution Committee, chaired by the CIO, reviews new investments, dispositions and follow-on transactions for approval; Finance oversees valuation processes independently of investment departments, with the Valuation Committee (management) and Audit Committee (Board) governing valuation

sources.title: The model fund F2021 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2021)
sources.supports: PE has 166 direct investments and 160 manager relationships (F2021); the Direct Private Equity portfolio held 88 direct investments valued at C$53.3 billion; DPE invests alongside aligned partners; Funds and Secondaries makes minority, passive direct investments up to C$100 million alongside fund partners; Portfolio Value Creation supports active asset management of direct equity investments with material governance rights (value creation planning, evaluation and selection of senior management, board director selection and engagement, investment monitoring); the Investment Decision Committee approves follow-on transactions to existing investments under CEO-set Investment Management Authorities; DPE pursued follow-ons and supported two portfolio company IPOs in fiscal 2021

sources.title: The model fund 2020 Annual Report
sources.supports: PE had 152 direct investments and 152 manager relationships (F2020); DPE held 85 direct investments valued at C$38.0 billion; PVC assists in due diligence, enhances governance, actively monitors portfolio companies and drives operational change through value creation initiatives

sources.title: 2022 Report on Sustainable Investing
sources.supports: Onboarding and monitoring practices for assets with material governance rights (value creation planning, management and director evaluation, monitoring of company performance including sustainability factors); proprietary sustainability KPI framework for existing direct equity investments developed in fiscal 2022; cyber maturity assessment of direct equity portfolio companies; Climate Change Security Selection Framework applied to existing assets; joined the ESG Data Convergence Initiative in fall 2021; engagement through board representation

sources.title: What Do Private Equity Firms Say They Do? (NBER Working Paper 21133)
sources.publisher: Gompers, Kaplan and Mukharlyamov, National Bureau of Economic Research
sources.supports: Survey of 79 PE investors: over 90% of portfolio company boards have 5 to 7 members; operating partners are involved in post-investment value creation in 51% of deals and outside consultants in 27%; sources of added value in order are revenue growth, incentives and governance, a high-value exit, additional acquisitions, replacing management and cost cuts; holding periods centre on about five years

sources.title: Standard board meeting cadence (Private equity board member handbook)
sources.supports: Many PE-backed boards meet 6 to 10 times a year, most often every 6 to 8 weeks, with four meetings a year as the minimum; management circulates the board pack 3 to 7 days before the meeting and directors need at least two hours to read it; meetings run 2 to 4 hours; next year's budget is discussed in September and October, finalised in November and December and signed off in January and February

sources.title: PE portfolio reporting requirements
sources.supports: Sponsors typically require a monthly flash within 3 to 10 business days, a full monthly management pack 10 to 20 business days after month end with variance commentary and cash reporting, a KPI schedule tied to the investment thesis, a quarterly covenant compliance certificate often due 45 days after quarter end, a quarterly board pack 5 to 7 days before the meeting and an annual budget before the fiscal year starts

sources.title: Principal, Sustainable Energies (job posting, the model fund, New York)
sources.supports: The model fund principals oversee the financial and operating performance of portfolio companies, sit on portfolio company boards as members or observers, prepare internal materials on portfolio company updates and recommendations, lead portfolio company valuation analyses and build operating models

sources.title: Replacing Excel for KPI analysis?
sources.publisher: Canadian Venture Capital and Private Equity Association (CVCA Central)
sources.supports: Private equity firms track portfolio company KPIs mostly in Excel; reports are assembled from several systems by hand, which wastes hours and creates differences between source systems and the Excel report

sources.title: International Private Equity and Venture Capital Valuation Guidelines (December 2018 edition)
sources.supports: Fair value of each investment assessed at each measurement date; valuation inputs calibrated to the entry price; backtesting of realised exits against prior estimates

sources.title: 2020 GIPS Standards for Asset Owners
sources.supports: Private market investment portfolios valued at least quarterly as of each quarter end (22.A.30)

sources.title: the fund's governing act (S.C. 1997, c. 40), sections 47 to 52
sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: Quarterly financial statements must be sent to the ministers within 45 days after the quarter (s. 50(1)), which sets the deadline for quarter-end valuation inputs

assumptions: The unit is one holding-quarter. The case starts when the first monthly pack of the quarter arrives (about 20 days into the second month) and runs through the quarter-end pack, valuation inputs and the board meeting to the quarterly portfolio review, so consecutive cases overlap by a few weeks.

Mix of holding-quarters: 62% active holdings with a board seat or material governance rights, 33% passive co-investments followed through the sponsor, 5% newly closed holdings in their first quarter. This is the author's split of the 166 direct investments reported in F2021 (88 in DPE).

The deal team's proposal of a quarter-end value and the valuation challenge are in fin-quarterly-valuation; this workflow stops at sending the inputs. The valuation workflow expects deal team proposals about ten days after quarter end, earlier than the quarter-end packs assumed here (two to three weeks after quarter end); in practice teams use flash results.

Follow-on requests leave this workflow as a new pipeline opportunity (step s15). The process map has no link from this process to screening or committee approval for follow-ons, which is a gap in the organisation file.

Hands-on times count focused work only. At 50 holding-quarters a month they imply about 14 FTE and the roles state about 14 FTE, roughly 15% of the 95 people in the direct and Asia groups, who also run new deals and exits. Informal contact with management and travel are not counted, so real time on portfolio work is likely higher.

The simulated median (about 70 days) sits slightly above the 65-day benchmark reading because the simulator adds the wait for the board pack after the valuation inputs in sequence; passive co-investments close in about two weeks and pull the overall distribution down only below the median.
Board meetings are counted once per quarter; extra meetings at boards that meet six to ten times a year are folded into the director's time range.
Loaded costs per hour are the organisation file's (total compensation scaled to F2022 personnel expense, times an overhead factor of 1.25, divided by 1,950 hours).
pvc_principal is in the process map's role list for the value creation link; si_specialist work on sustainability data is folded into the associate's step s18 rather than added as a role.
